panels.title: What the provider is billing for
Tokens per second, by direction
panels.description: Spring AI's own meter. Input and output are priced differently by every provider, so they are never summed. The label is gen_ai_token_type: input, output, total — 'total' is the provider's own sum and double-counts if added to the other two.

panels.title: Tokens per second, by model
panels.description: Which model is actually consuming the budget. A route change that costs more shows up here before it shows up on an invoice.

panels.title: Tokens per second attributed to a pipeline stage
panels.description: OrgMemory's own meter, not Spring AI's. Spring AI attributes cost to a model; this attributes it to the stage that spent it — extraction versus gleaning versus generation. Neither derives the other, which is why both exist.

panels.title: Model call latency
panels.description: Spring AI observes inside ChatModel, below OrgMemory's port, so this is the provider call alone — it excludes permission-scoped retrieval. For what the user waits through, see the Assistant board.

panels.title: Model calls per second, by operation and model
Answers cut short by the token limit

options.content:
`finish_reason` is a **span** attribute, not a metric — Spring AI records `gen_ai.response.finish_reasons` on the `gen_ai.client.operation` span and exports no counter for it.

So it is a trace query, not a panel here. In **Explore → Tempo**:

```
{ span.gen_ai.response.finish_reasons =~ ".*length.*" }
```

A rising count of those means answers are being truncated by the model's own output limit, which no latency or token chart shows.

One upstream caveat worth knowing before reading these panels: `gen_ai.system` is deprecated in OpenTelemetry semantic conventions in favour of `gen_ai.provider.name`, and Spring AI has not migrated (`spring-projects/spring-ai#6668`, unresolved). This board avoids depending on it.
